questions.question: A job sequencing model schedules several jobs on a single machine. Which description fits this model?
options: Jobs run one at a time without interruption; the total of the completion times is minimized
Jobs run one at a time without interruption; total weighted tardiness is minimized
Jobs may be interrupted and resumed later; total weighted tardiness is minimized
Jobs may run at the same time on the machine; total weighted tardiness is minimized

questions.question: In a job sequencing model, job $i$ has start $s_i$ and processing time $p_i$, and for each pair $i<j$ the constraints $s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij})$ and $s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}$ with $y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$. What does $y_{12}=1$ impose?
options: Job 1 starts before job 2, but the two may overlap
Job 1 precedes job 2: $s_1+p_1\le s_2$ must hold
Both $s_1+p_1\le s_2$ and $s_2+p_2\le s_1$ must hold
Jobs 1 and 2 may overlap, as long as both finish

questions.question: In a job sequencing model with start $s_i\ge0$, processing time $p_i$, due date $d_i$, tardiness $T_i\ge0$ and penalty rate $w_i$, tardiness satisfies $T_i\ge s_i+p_i-d_i$. A job finishes 3 time units before its due date. What penalty does it incur?
options: A bonus of $3w_i$, as its lateness is $-3$
A penalty of $3w_i$, for missing the due date by 3
A penalty of $w_i$, as every job costs its rate
A penalty of 0, since $T_i=0$ for early completion

questions.question: A job sequencing model uses binary precedence variables $y_{ij}$, continuous start times $s_i\ge0$ and continuous tardiness variables $T_i\ge0$. Which class of model is it?
options: A linear program, as every constraint is linear in the variables
A pure integer program, as the order of the jobs is a discrete choice
A mixed integer program, as binary and continuous variables coexist
A binary program, as every variable only records a yes/no choice

questions.question: In a job sequencing model with tardiness $T_i\ge s_i+p_i-d_i$ and $T_i\ge0$, a job starts at $s_i=10$, takes $p_i=6$ and is due at $d_i=12$. What is its tardiness at an optimal solution with positive penalty rate?
Two jobs on one machine have processing times $p=(3,5)$, due dates $d=(4,6)$ and penalty rates $w=(2,1)$. Without idle time, which order minimizes total weighted tardiness, and at what penalty?
options: Job 1 first, with penalty 2
Job 2 first, with penalty 8
Job 1 first, with penalty 4
Job 2 first, with penalty 0

questions.question: A job sequencing model for 4 jobs uses one binary variable $y_{ij}$ with its pair of constraints for each pair $i<j$. How many binary precedence variables does it have?

In a job sequencing model with for each pair $i<j$ the constraints $s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij})$ and $s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}$ with $y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$, why are there two constraints per pair, one with $M(1-y_{ij})$ and one with $My_{ij}$?
options: Both orders are enforced together, so no two jobs can overlap
Neither order is enforced; the constraints only bound the start times
Each value of $y_{ij}$ enforces one order and relaxes the other
Two constraints are needed because $M$ must appear twice in the objective

questions.question: In a job sequencing model, only $T_i\ge s_i+p_i-d_i$ and $T_i\ge0$ link tardiness to the schedule, and the objective $\sum_iw_iT_i$ is minimized with all $w_i>0$. Why is $T_i=\max(0,s_i+p_i-d_i)$ at an optimum?
options: The two constraints force $T_i$ to equal that maximum
The equality holds at every feasible solution of the model
The equality holds only for jobs that finish late
The objective pushes $T_i$ down until a lower bound binds

questions.question: In a job sequencing model with nonnegative penalty rates, a feasible schedule leaves the machine idle between two jobs. Why can a schedule without idle time be at least as good?
options: Idle time is already forbidden by the pairwise constraints
Removing idle time always makes every job on time
Idle time raises the penalty rates of later jobs
Starting later jobs earlier never increases any tardiness

questions.question: Three jobs on one machine have processing times $p=(5,20,15)$, due dates $d=(24,22,35)$ and penalty rates $w=(19,12,34)$ for jobs 1, 2, 3. The jobs are run in the order 1, 2, 3 without idle time. What is the total weighted tardiness penalty?
In a job sequencing model with three jobs, $y_{ij}=1$ means job $i$ precedes job $j$ (for $i<j$). Which values encode the sequence 2, 1, 3?

In a job sequencing model with for each pair $i<j$ the constraints $s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij})$ and $s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}$ with $y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$, a proposed solution has $y_{12}=1$, $s_1=0$, $p_1=5$, $s_2=3$ and $p_2=4$. Is it feasible for this pair?
options: No: $s_2+p_2\le s_1+M$ fails, as $7>0$
Yes: the jobs start at different times
Yes: the term with $M$ absorbs the overlap
No: $s_1+p_1\le s_2$ fails, since $5>3$

questions.question: In a job sequencing model with for each pair $i<j$ the constraints $s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij})$ and $s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}$ with $y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$, the modeller picks $M$ much smaller than the scheduling horizon. What can go wrong?
options: The jobs can overlap, as the active inequality is weakened
Nothing, since $y_{ij}$ alone decides the order of the jobs
The relaxed inequality may still cut off valid schedules
The model becomes infeasible for every choice of $M$

questions.question: In a job sequencing model with start $s_i\ge0$, processing time $p_i$, due date $d_i$, tardiness $T_i\ge0$ and penalty rate $w_i$, the constraint $T_i\ge0$ is dropped, leaving only $T_i\ge s_i+p_i-d_i$. What changes?
options: Nothing, since a tardiness value can never be negative anyway
Early jobs get negative $T_i$, so earliness is rewarded
The model becomes infeasible for every schedule
Late jobs are no longer charged in the objective

questions.question: Three jobs on one machine have processing times $p=(5,20,15)$, due dates $d=(24,22,35)$ and penalty rates $w=(19,12,34)$ for jobs 1, 2, 3. With $M=20$, is the schedule $s_2=0$, $s_1=20$, $s_3=25$ with $y_{12}=0$, $y_{13}=1$, $y_{23}=1$ feasible for the pairwise constraints $s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij})$ and $s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}$ ($i<j$, $y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$)?
options: Yes: every active inequality, such as $20\le20$, holds here
No: $25\le20$ fails for pair (1,2), $40\le20$ for (2,3)
No, but only pair (2,3) fails, as $40\le0+20$ is false
No: job 3 breaks its tardiness bound, as $40>35$
